acf.summary: A new brand and proposition for NPTN by LMS, a bold new approach to transforming the way property transactions happen. We created a brand that makes complex infrastructure feel simple, human, and full of momentum, built around one powerful idea: collaboration that rewires the system.
acf.sub_title: Urban Alchemy
acf.info_title: People. Places. Purpose
acf.info_overview:
Cheltenham is more than four extraordinary days of racing. It is anticipation building from the moment you arrive. The pressure before the first race. The roar rolling through the stands. History, rivalry, celebration, relief and pure release all happening in the same place.
A few years ago, we distilled that into a simple campaign thought ‘Nothing Feels like Cheltenham.’ For 2027, now the third year of the platform, the opportunity was not to reinvent it, but to get even closer to the truth behind it.

So we went to the Festival and captured it for real.

Across the four days, we filmed and photographed the moments that make Cheltenham what it is – not simply the racing, but the faces, nerves, style, friendships, reactions and sudden explosions of emotion around it. The approach gives the 2027 campaign a rawer, more immersive quality: less observation, more feeling.

We also wanted Cheltenham to become as distinctive to the ear as it is to the eye. Working with specialist sound partners, we recorded the sounds and atmosphere of the Festival and used them to inspire a bespoke piece of music for TV and social. Alongside it, we developed a dedicated sonic identity that can live across the wider Cheltenham estate – creating a recognisable audio signature that can grow in familiarity year after year.

The campaign brings photography, film, language, music and sound together around one emotional idea, while a flexible suite of templates and systems gives the internal Jockey Club design team the tools to roll it out consistently across day-to-day communications.

The aim for 2027 is simple: not just to show people Cheltenham.
To make them feel it.

acf.sub_title: Connecting people, place and possibility.
acf.info_title: Creating an identity that connects people, place and possibility.

At the heart of Birmingham, Centre City represents a new approach to urban working. With its striking refurbishment, premium wellness facilities and collaborative spaces, Bruntwood SciTech set out to create more than an exceptional workplace – a destination where people and businesses could connect, thrive and grow.

Our creative approach centred on the idea of connection. We developed a minimal, contemporary visual identity built around a distinctive, intertwined ‘C’ symbol – an organic expression of the building’s relationship with the city and the connections formed within its walls. The fluid, interconnected mark reflects both Centre City’s unrivalled connectivity, moments from New Street Station, and its commitment to bringing businesses and people together. Combined with refined typography and a confident visual language, the identity balances commercial sophistication with a more human, welcoming character.

The result is a distinctive, future-facing brand that establishes Centre City as more than a place to work – a place to connect, collaborate and grow.

acf.caption: NPTN Brand Development
acf.summary: A new brand and proposition for NPTN by LMS, a bold new approach to transforming the way property transactions happen. We created a brand that makes complex infrastructure feel simple, human, and full of momentum, built around one powerful idea: collaboration that rewires the system.
acf.sub_title: Rewiring the future of property transactions
acf.info_title: Rewiring the future of property transactions
acf.info_overview:
The way we buy and sell homes is broken. For NPTN, the ambition was to change that, connecting lenders, law firms, estate agents, brokers, technology providers, and customers through one smarter flow of data.

Our challenge was to make a complex piece of industry infrastructure feel immediate and compelling. Rather than presenting NPTN as another platform or technology product, we positioned it as a fundamental shift in how the property market works: open, connected, faster, and built for everyone.

The visual identity is brought to life through a dynamic world of connected forms, movement and data. A flexible graphic system gives the brand a sense of constant flow, while bold typography and confident messaging make the proposition clear without losing the human story behind it.

The result is a brand designed not simply to launch a new network, but to help move an entire industry forward. Because NPTN isn’t about digitising the existing system. It’s about rebuilding it for what comes next.

acf.caption: Annual Conference Branding
acf.summary: A transformative brand and campaign concept for the BCO Annual Conference 2026 in Edinburgh – the world’s capital of creativity, knowledge, and innovation. We reimagined the future of workplace thinking, bringing together design, strategy, and storytelling under one unifying theme: ‘A Festival of Enlightenment’.
acf.sub_title: Transforming a conference into an experience.
acf.info_title: Transforming a conference into an experience.
acf.info_overview:
For BCO 2026, the task was to elevate a traditional industry event into a festival of collaboration, learning, and inspiration – one that truly reflects Edinburgh’s spirit of progress and the BCO’s leadership in shaping the workplace of tomorrow.

Our creative concept, ‘A Festival of Enlightenment’, was born from Edinburgh’s legacy as the heart of the Scottish Enlightenment – a city where ideas changed the world. The brand narrative mirrors this spirit, positioning the modern office as more than a place to work, but a place to connect, innovate, and evolve.

The identity fuses heritage and modernity: a confident, geometric visual system inspired by Edinburgh’s architecture and energy, built around dynamic ‘E’ symbol to convey both structure and transformation. A rich palette rooted in the city’s landscape – from Forth Bridge Red to Leith Sunshine, balances timeless sophistication with festival vibrancy.

From brand identity to digital activation and event design, the concept captures what the BCO stands for: progress, collaboration, and enlightenment. A celebration not just of where we work – but how we think, learn, and grow together.

be-part-of-sports-greatest-story.post_title: Be part of sport’s greatest story

acf.caption: Grand National Festival Campaign
acf.summary: A bold creative platform that captured the scale, emotion and storytelling power of one of the world’s greatest sporting events. Built around the line ‘Be part of sport’s greatest story’ the campaign invited audiences to immerse themselves in a festival where every moment adds to a living legend.
acf.sub_title: Capturing the power and emotion of an icon.
acf.info_title: Capturing the power and emotion of an icon.
acf.info_overview:
The Randox Grand National Festival is far more than the world’s greatest steeplechase – it’s an experience where stories become legends and unforgettable moments are etched into history.

The campaign celebrated that truth turning anticipation, atmosphere and emotion into a unified creative idea. ‘Be part of sport’s greatest story’ became the heartbeat of the festival, inspiring audiences to not just watch, but to be part of something extraordinary. We gave each of the three days its own narrative and character, reflecting the rhythm and emotion of the event as it builds towards the ultimate race. We developed headline copy and storytelling across OOH, digital, social and print as well as scripting and producing the TV advert, which featured a voiceover from film and theatre royalty David Morrisey.

The creative framework and messaging foundation empowered The Jockey Club’s internal team to deliver consistent emotionally charged communications across every channel and audience touchpoint – setting a new tone for the festival’s story to be told.

blocks.quote: “We’ve been delighted to work with Loaf alongside our existing team to bring together the concept ‘Be Part of Sport’s Greatest Story’ – they approached the brief with a huge amount of passion and drive to support us in creating something that resonated with our audiences. As a result we saw key engagement increases across multiple channels, a record year for ticketing revenues and a 59% increase in 18-24 year old bookers. We’ve also been nominated for industry awards across both Horse Racing and wider Sport as a result of a successful campaign and event.”
blocks.meta: James Rennard, Head of Marketing (Aintree & Haydock Park) - The Jockey Club

acf.caption: Crescent Salford Placemaking
acf.sub_title: Capturing the energy of a city with huge potential.
acf.summary: English Cities Fund, University of Salford, and Salford City Council came together to reimagine the centre of Salford and deliver urban regeneration at unprecedented scale. They needed a distinct brand that ushered this community into the future without losing sight of Salford’s past and pride.
acf.info_title: Capturing the energy of a city with huge potential.
acf.info_overview:
Crescent Salford has the potential to act as a catalyst for further growth and prosperity. The masterplan celebrates its people and demonstrates real investment in a better future. It places community, sustainability, and innovation at its centre. This project needed a single guiding thought to drive the brand forward. We started with deep stakeholder engagement across the public and private sector to understand what makes Salford tick. Ultimately we found it—this project was an opportunity for people to make progress. It was all about ‘moving forward together.’

Salford has a rich history of innovation and we wanted to capture that passion and ingenuity in this flexible and confident brand. In this project we celebrate the present while setting Salford up for the future. We delivered a bold brand that reflects Crescent’s vision and heritage and set up tools for its teams to put it to good use throughout the consultations, marketing, and placemaking stages of development.

blocks.quote: “Loaf was selected following a rigorous selection process. All the partners have been impressed with Loaf’s ability to craft vision into reality and we are currently working to deliver a brand that blends both the proud heritage of the city with its aspirations for the future.”
blocks.meta: Carly Jones, Brand and Marketing Manager - Muse Developments - ECF

acf.caption: Spring Campaign
acf.summary: A campaign designed to position Merseyrail as the ultimate facilitator of springtime adventures across the Liverpool City Region. ‘Make Your Spring' invited audiences to explore and make more of the season – powered by the convenience, reliability, and affordability of Merseyrail.
acf.sub_title: Bringing the joy of spring to life, one journey at a time.
acf.info_title: Bringing the joy of spring to life, one journey at a time.
acf.info_overview:
‘Make Your Spring’ captured the spirit of new beginnings – a time when the city comes alive, the weather warms, and people are ready to get out and explore. Built around Merseyrail’s award-winning service and brand-new trains, the campaign reminded customers that their next great day out starts on board.

The creative brought a handcrafted, scrapbook feel to life – celebrating individuality and the idea of ‘making’ your own perfect spring. Every journey could be uniquely yours, whether that’s hopping between seaside towns, visiting family, or discovering local gems with friends.

Supporting digital activations, influencer partnerships, and user-generated content extended the campaign’s reach, encouraging passengers to share how they were ‘making their spring’ with Merseyrail.

Through vivid design, relatable storytelling and a sense of fun, the campaign elevated off-peak travel from an everyday choice to an open invitation to embark on adventures, create memories, and make the most of the season with Merseyrail.

acf.caption: SOLP Placemaking
acf.sub_title: Actioning an Olympic Legacy.
acf.summary: Sheffield Olympic Legacy Park was entering a new phase of development driven forward by Scarborough International Group. After a decade of successful partnerships and investment, this next stage of commercial growth required a strong and distinctive brand rooted in an active legacy.
acf.info_title: Actioning an Olympic Legacy.
acf.info_overview:
The London 2012 Olympic and Paralympic Games set a global stage for the UK and Sheffield. A legacy of sport, health, access, and opportunity. Sheffield Olympic Legacy Park is putting that legacy to work as the only Olympic legacy park outside of a host city. The brand needed to accommodate community engagement, research and innovation, education, commercial development and more. Our solution was rooted in what makes the Olympics great: proximity, performance, and potential.

With investment in commercial innovation, research, and education, this is a place ‘made to move’. The brand captures the energy and enthusiasm of elite sport without excluding the person next door. Sheffield Olympic Legacy Park is ready to take its place on the national and global stage as an exemplar place for world-class innovation in sport, health and wellbeing.

Not only that but their creative outputs are fresh, innovative and really reflect the ethos of the brand.”

acf.info_title: Building credibility in an established market.
acf.info_overview:
In a crowded market dominated by established national players, the challenge was clear – build instant credibility, create emotional connection, and stand out with purpose.

The ‘Golden Ticket’ was Jumbo Interactive’s first foray into the UK prize market, after 20 years of delivering worldwide lottery solutions. Rooted in positivity and authenticity, the brand and campaign brought to life the feeling of opportunity – a golden moment where ordinary people could win extraordinary prizes, all while helping causes that matter.

Through bold, joyful creative and a consistent golden theme, the campaign owned a space of optimism and generosity. Supported by paid social, PPC, PR, Charity partnerships and influencer activation, it built awareness fast while driving direct ticket sales and adoption. A feel-good revolution in the UK prize draw market.

acf.caption: Leisure Campaign
acf.summary: We worked with Merseyrail to help deliver their 2025 leisure campaign, built around one powerful idea – Merseyrail takes you there. A creative platform designed to connect emotion and experience, showing that how you travel shapes how you feel when you arrive.
acf.sub_title: Showing that a better journey makes for a better day.
acf.info_title: Showing that a better journey makes for a better day.
acf.info_overview:
The campaign set out to change perceptions of everyday travel – turning the train from a functional choice into an emotional one. If your journey is stressful – your day starts that way. But when you travel with Merseyrail, you arrive calm, connected and ready to enjoy every moment.

The double meaning of ‘Merseyrail takes you there’ captures both the physical act of travel and the feeling of being in those memorable, enjoyable moments. Photography and headlines reinforced this connection – showing genuine emotion and enjoyment made possible by an easy, stress-free journey.

The approach reinforced the idea that the experience of getting there and being there are inseparable. A confident design system built around Merseyrail’s iconic yellow and simple typography gave clarity and optimism to every execution across all four seasons. The campaign reminded people that Merseyrail doesn’t just take you places – it makes every trip better.

acf.caption: Healthcare Conference Branding
acf.summary: We partnered with GS1 UK Healthcare to bring their Annual Conference to life – creating a new event identity, tagline and immersive design system built around the theme ‘Safer, smarter, connected healthcare’. From branding to spatial experience – we reimagined the event as a live embodiment of GS1’s mission to enhance safety efficiency and collaboration across the healthcare ecosystem.
acf.sub_title: Transforming a conference into a connected experience.
acf.info_title: Transforming a conference into a connected experience.
acf.info_overview:
Our task was to elevate the GS1 UK Healthcare Conference into an engaging, future-focused event that would demonstrate how GS1 standards transform healthcare delivery. Inspired by their purpose of ‘harnessing the power of standards to transform the way people work and live’, our creative approach centred on human connection, innovation and collaboration.

The event identity visualised connectivity through dynamic gradients and barcode-inspired motion graphics – used across digital presentations, animations and on-site displays. A modular toolkit unified everything from stage sets and signage to social content and delegate materials.

To enhance engagement we designed two experiential walls encouraging hands-on interaction and storytelling within the space. The result was a seamless modern environment that made complex data feel human, accessible and alive – showcasing GS1’s leadership in shaping a safer, smarter, and more connected future for healthcare.

blocks.quote: “Thank you to the amazing team for your brilliant ideas, inspiration and for letting us be the best we could possibly be together – all within a crazy short time.”
blocks.meta: Glen Hodgson, Head of Healthcare - GS1 UK

acf.caption: Contour Branding & Website
acf.summary: Contour is a 51-storey residential tower in Manchester’s New Jackson neighbourhood embodying elegance and refinement. Renaker sought a brand that would mould the existing culture of the neighbourhood with the unique, refined character of this luxury development.
acf.sub_title: Crafting luxury living in the sky
acf.info_title: Crafting luxury living in the sky
acf.info_overview:
Contour was a crucial project in the wider masterplan for the thriving New Jackson neighbourhood. Its iconic chamfered architecture, and high-end, sophisticated interiors meant it would be one of Renaker’s most esteemed, luxurious developments so far.

The brand strategy and identity needed to be respectful of the New Jackson neighbourhood and adjacent buildings, whilst still establishing a strong, unique living destination. Our approach included naming the building and creating a minimal, refined identity, inspired by its design and Manchester’s industrial heritage.

Contour seamlessly integrates with its surroundings while standing out as a unique and prestigious living destination.

blocks.quote: “Loaf understood the brief and our vision for Contour. The result is very strong creative work which perfectly complemented the bold exterior design of the building and the elegant interiors and amenity spaces. The result is cohesive and striking collateral which translated very well onto the website Loaf designed. The Loaf team worked really well with our in-house marketing team”
blocks.meta: Martina Collins, Sales & Marketing Director - Renaker

acf.caption: Integral Branding
acf.summary: We partnered with Scarborough Group International to name, position and brand their new industrial offer at Thorpe Park Leeds – a pioneering concept designed to put people and purpose at the heart of production. Integral represents a shift from specification to human experience.
acf.sub_title: Defining the future of industrial spaces
acf.info_title: Defining the future of industrial spaces
acf.info_overview:
Scarborough Group International’s vision was bold – to challenge perceptions of the industrial sector, and design spaces that enhance productivity wellbeing and sustainability.Through insight and research we uncovered an opportunity to position these spaces as catalysts for both business growth and human progress.

The result was Integral – a name that captures the brand’s purpose: integral to success, community and people. Visually the identity connects two worlds – the square for structure, performance and precision – the circle for humanity, wellness and balance. Together they create a distinctive symbol of integration and innovation.

With clean typography a confident tone, the brand communicates a modern, holistic approach to industry – where people and productivity thrive together.

acf.caption: West Gate Brand Development
acf.summary: A distinctive brand identity for West Gate by Renaker – a landmark new residence at the western gateway to Deansgate, Manchester. We brought together the character of the River Irwell, the creative energy of St John’s, and a more refined vision of city-centre living to create a brand with a sense of place, culture, and permanence.
acf.sub_title: A landmark residence born of connection
acf.info_title: A landmark residence born of connection
acf.info_overview:
West Gate occupies a rare position in Manchester, where the curve of the River Irwell meets the cultural momentum of St John’s. Our challenge was to capture that intersection and translate it into a luxury residential brand that felt distinctive, considered, and genuinely connected to its surroundings.

Rather than treating the development as simply another collection of luxury apartments, we built the story around the relationship between the river and the city. Heritage meets contemporary design. Calm meets energy. Industry meets creativity.

The resulting identity takes cues from the architecture and landscape around West Gate, combining refined typography, considered composition, rich materials, and an atmospheric visual language. The brand feels premium without being overstated, creating a sense of quiet confidence that reflects both the development and its setting.

The storytelling brings the wider neighbourhood into focus too. West Gate sits within a part of Manchester shaped by industry, artistry, culture, and constant reinvention – a history that gives the contemporary development its sense of character.

From the brand identity through to the wider sales and marketing experience, every element was designed to communicate a particular kind of city living: elevated, connected, and considered.

A residence shaped by its surroundings, and a brand designed to make that connection felt.

acf.caption: Customer Behaviour Campaign
acf.summary: ‘We Race Together’ is a unifying campaign, designed to connect every customer interaction – from the racecourse to the call centre – through one clear message of inclusion, safety and shared responsibility. The initiative reframes The Jockey Club’s customer standards into a single positive commitment: that every experience is made better when we all race together.
acf.sub_title: Building a culture of respect, safety and community
acf.info_title: Building a culture of respect, safety and community
acf.info_overview:
As The Jockey Club introduced new policies around zero tolerance, complaints and customer service, the goal was to embed them within a meaningful customer-facing brand and campaign. The challenge was to shift behaviour and improve experiences, while maintaining warmth, respect and authority.

Our solution ‘We Race Together’ captured that balance – positioning respect, safety and great service as a shared promise between The Jockey Club and its audiences. The identity and tone were designed to be positive and inclusive, but with the strength to deliver firm messaging where needed. We developed the full messaging framework, tone of voice and campaign toolkit, giving The Jockey Club’s internal teams the flexibility to deliver consistent communication across all racecourses and channels.

Supporting this, a brand video brought the initiative to life – clearly outlining its purpose, policies and customer impact through emotive storytelling and bold visual design. The result was a confident organisation-wide foundation that championed community, accountability and care, helping everyone involved in racing feel part of something bigger.

blocks.quote: “The team at Loaf did an excellent job, combining creative and strategic thinking and quick, effective delivery on what was a complex project in a very tight timescale. I’d have no hesitation in using them again and indeed recommending them to others; they are a great example of just how useful and additive agencies can be to in-house resource and are a pleasure to work with.”
blocks.meta: Joe Rendall, Head of Strategic Communications - The Jockey Club

youre-ticket-to-an-epic-summer.post_title: Your ticket to an epic summer

acf.homepage_title_override:
Your ticket to an

acf.caption: Leisure Campaign
acf.summary: A campaign built to position Merseyrail as the ultimate gateway to an extraordinary and unforgettable summer and Christmas. The campaign inspired and captivated audiences, focussing on the experience of train travel and it’s benefits.
acf.sub_title: Unleashing the ‘magic’ of train travel
acf.info_title: Putting the customers and the experience first.
acf.info_overview: Unleashing the magic of Merseyrail’s off-peak tickets, the campaign visuals depict off-peak tickets transporting passengers effortlessly across the Liverpool region. Built on the pillars of reliability, affordability, speed, and stress-free travel, the campaign takes Merseyrail’s unique selling points and weaves them into a magical ‘experience’ narrative.The core message encapsulates the essence of hassle-free travel, encouraging individuals and families to embark on unforgettable experiences without the worry of traffic, delays, or high costs. The idea had to work seamlessly across both Summer and Christmas periods.The campaign inspired and captivated audiences, focussing on the experience of train travel – engaging customers in a more experiential and emotional way. It drove record numbers of customers to the website and drove a 15% year on year increase in revenue for leisure travel.

blocks.quote: “We are delighted with the work that Loaf have created for our summer campaign. A positive and bright strategy has been creatively brought to life, not only showcasing the practical benefits of our train service but cleverly positioning Merseyrail as an attraction in itself. It’s a campaign that helps boost our brand recognition whilst also including an all-important sales pitch to thousands of potential customers throughout the Liverpool City Region.”

acf.caption: Cheltenham Festival Campaign
acf.summary: ‘Nothing Feels Like Cheltenham’ is a bold, emotionally charged campaign that celebrates the unique energy, anticipation, and spirit of the world famous Cheltenham Festival. A creative platform built to connect audiences not just to the racing - but to the feeling of being there.
acf.sub_title: Capturing the emotion of an icon
acf.info_title: Capturing the emotion behind the world’s greatest jump racing festival.
acf.info_overview:
The Cheltenham Festival is more than four days of world-class racing – it’s a sensory experience like no other. From the thunder of hooves to the roar of the crowd, every moment is alive with drama, passion, and pride. Our task was to capture that feeling in a way that would inspire fans, unite audiences, and reignite the Festival’s emotional heartbeat.

The campaign line ‘Nothing Feels Like Cheltenham’ became a rallying cry, expressing the intensity, joy, and anticipation that make this event truly iconic. We created a full creative framework, developing master visuals for each of the four days – Champion Day, Ladies Day St Patrick’s Thursday and Gold Cup Day – each celebrating its own distinctive character and emotion.

Supporting imagery, social films, animations, and BVOD assets extended the story across every touchpoint, ensuring consistency and impact throughout the campaign’s lifecycle. To bring authenticity and craft to every execution, we developed a bespoke handwritten typeface – adding texture, individuality, and emotion to the visual identity.

The campaign culminated in a powerful TV advert – an immersive celebration of everything that makes The Cheltenham Festival unlike anything else in sport. Because when you’re there, you don’t just watch it… you feel it.

acf.caption: Rondex Branding
acf.summary: Davis & Moore, a renowned name in industrial cleaning solutions, approached us with a compelling challenge: to create a distinctive and modern brand for their new line of premium industrial wipes. Challenge accepted.
acf.sub_title: Delivering a premium vision
acf.info_title: Setting a new standard in industrial wipes
acf.info_overview: The foundation of our branding project was a thorough understanding of the market and the specific needs of Davis & Moore’s target audience. Our strategy focused on positioning Rondex as the go-to choice for clients who demanded excellence in more than just the product.‘Predictably premium wipes’ is not just a brand essence, it’s a commitment to consistently delivering on the promise of quality, consistency and reliability, and was delivered by the tagline ‘Precision in every wipe’ – an embodiment of that commitment.The colour palette, typography and overall design aesthetic were crafted to reflect the premium but industrial nature of the brand, and we subtly reinforced the product’s core function through the logo design. The brand was brought to life though 3D animation, microsite, video and packaging design.

acf.caption: Branding & Website
acf.summary: A full-spectrum brand and workflow redesign for Navy & Grey – the award-winning creative audio studio that fuses deep AI insight with human creativity. This project reshaped how the brand works internally, how it shows up externally, and how it delivers outstanding audio-driven experiences for clients.
acf.sub_title: Audio creativity delivered with clarity
acf.info_title: Audio creativity delivered with clarity
acf.info_overview:
In a rapidly evolving audio-and-voice landscape, Navy & Grey needed a brand identity and operational workflow that could keep pace with their innovation – from AI-driven insight to human-led creative execution. Our partnership delivered exactly that.

We began by mapping out their workflow – from how ideas flow, into production and delivery, and we refined every hand-off, touchpoint and tool in that chain. The outcome was a streamlined, smarter process built for speed, clarity and impact.

Parallel to the workflow redesign, we overhauled the brand guidelines and website. The refreshed identity reflects their unique position: bold, human creativity, anchored in data and technology. Visuals, tone of voice, colour and typography all align to support a brand that is intelligent, inventive and accessible.

With a consistent identity and refined workflow, Navy & Grey now show up with confidence – internally aligned and externally distinctive, and ready to supercharge brand audio experiences for the next chapter.

acf.caption: Internal Campaign
acf.summary: Assaults on police officers are a serious matter with potentially devastating consequences. National Police Wellbeing Service ‘Oscar Kilo’, enlisted our help to launch a campaign that would aid their national effort to enhance the support provided to victims of assault and improve their response to such incidents.
acf.sub_title: Raising awareness of a national support initiative.
acf.info_title: Raising awareness of a national support initiative.
acf.info_overview:
Our “together against assaults” campaign sought to ignite a spark and shed light on the issue of assaults, raising awareness and encouraging more officers and staff to join the conversation. We knew that to truly make a change, we needed to involve those on the front lines and give them a sense of ownership in the campaign.

Assaults should never be accepted as ‘just part of the job’. Our approach was grounded in the belief that a shift in culture and a united mentality were key to breaking the silence and fostering a safer environment for all. Our unique approach and execution, led by project ambassador Rav Wilding, led to positive conversations and an embrace of the campaign right from launch.

blocks.quote: “Loaf have been fantastic to work with – from the very start of the concept creation, right through the execution and delivery of the campaign. They quickly picked up on the brief and understood the unique challenges we were trying to address. The team provided some real creativity to our thinking and we’ve ended up with a really impactful campaign that we believe will have real longevity.”
blocks.meta: Jenna Flanagan, Communications and Engagement Manager - Oscar Kilo / National Police Wellbeing Service

acf.caption: Crescent Innovation Branding
acf.sub_title: Applied innovation in motion.
acf.summary: English Cities Fund, University of Salford, and Salford City Council devised an innovation district with a clear focus. Unlike the exclusive science parks of the past, this is a place with open access to opportunities. They needed a brand that captured its dedication to practical application.
acf.info_title: Applied innovation in motion
acf.info_overview:
The Crescent Innovation’s brand was borne directly out of the Crescent Salford brand we had created, but we recognised that there was an opportunity to drive momentum and capture attention with custom brand elements that matched the scale of the opportunity. Our challenge was to adapt the master brand enough to build distinctive and differentiated assets without losing any shared brand equity.

We saw the incredible opportunity at the intersection of healthcare, robotics, automation and the built environment and sought to capture it with both the brand strategy, narrative and visual identity. Working with stakeholders across the public and private sector, we showcased the potential of this remarkable place where research and industry collide: Build smarter. Live better.

blocks.quote: “Loaf was selected following a rigorous selection process. All the partners have been impressed with Loaf’s ability to craft vision into reality and we are currently working to deliver a brand that blends both the proud heritage of the city with its aspirations for the future.”
blocks.meta: Carly Jones, Brand & Marketing Manager - ECF / Muse

acf.caption: Campaign
acf.sub_title: Promoting sustained health and wellbeing.
acf.summary: Total Fitness wanted to use the January period as an opportunity to enforce their belief that everyone is better fitter. A campaign to build the brand story in a way that would be distinctive and inclusive, far away from the usual call to put down the Christmas mince pies, and the ‘new year - new you’ narrative.
acf.info_title: Promoting sustained health and wellbeing.
acf.info_overview:
Total Fitness is the leading mid-market health club in the north, providing more ways to get fit, stay in shape and improve mental wellbeing than any of it’s direct competitors – with a solid support network, comfortable environment for all age groups, and online training service to boot.

Fitness shouldn’t be a pastime of a select, typical few. Mental and physical fitness is important for everyone, and it improves every part of our lives. The campaign ‘Fitter. My way’ delivered an inclusive message that whatever your goals, schedules, commitments, stage of fitness, physical and mental needs – Total Fitness could play a major role in the goal to get fitter – whilst re-defining what fitness actually is and isn’t.

acf.caption: Internal Campaign
acf.sub_title: Capturing the values shaping internal culture
acf.summary: An uplift in recruitment called for Lancashire Constabulary to revisit its brand values and internal communications strategy. But first, we needed to understand what makes the force tick.
acf.info_title: Capturing the values shaping internal culture
acf.info_overview:
Lancashire Constabulary approached us to help articulate their brand values. While the force’s ethics and code of conduct were clear, we needed to discover and articulate the emotive, cultural values that shaped the real experience of officers and staff.

We started with in-depth qualitative research, interviewing staff and stakeholders from across the organisation. The force’s role in the community was clear — there is a deep sense of pride in working to make Lancashire a better, and safer, place to live. We wanted to capture that energy to promote positive behaviours within the force, improve engagement, and align officers and staff behind a common purpose.

This campaign serves as the foundation for all internal communications moving forward. It reinforces the values that all officers and staff at Lancashire Constabulary should hold dear and act as guiding principles for how their teams work together.

blocks.quote: Loaf have been a breath of fresh air to work with, they guided us through the whole process which including leading on the research and insights stage and involving our staff in this right from the beginning. We could not have been happier with the final outcome.
blocks.meta: Sarah Gough / Internal Communications & Staff Engagement Manager / Lancs Police

acf.caption: Afflecks Brand Dev
acf.sub_title: Evolving a retail icon
acf.summary: Afflecks is legendary in Manchester. It’s a retail institution with a legacy of counter-culture, self-expression, and independence. They needed a new brand that paid tribute to its past whilst setting it up for the future.
acf.info_title: Evolving a retail icon
acf.info_overview: Manchester is a city ever changing — yet some things endure. Afflecks has been a beacon for independent thinking, community, and Mancunian pride for more than three decades. When Bruntwood approached us to refresh their brand identity, we felt energised by its potential. Afflecks is more than a retail destination, it’s a safe space for bold and brilliant entrepreneurs, consumers, thinkers, dreamers, and more. This is a place for the weird and wonderful. We built this identity from the patchwork of cultures, both alternative and mainstream, that exist in and around Afflecks. We wanted to capture the raw spirit of this place and pay tribute to the brilliant makers and traders driving its success.

acf.caption: Circle Square Campaign & Web
acf.sub_title: Placemaking a new neighbourhood in the heart of Manchester
acf.summary: A new neighbourhood in the making grounded by an ambitious idea: a place to enable the extraordinary. But how do you raise the profile of a place that doesn’t exist yet? By taking underrated media space to the limit.
acf.info_title: Placemaking a new neighbourhood in the heart of Manchester
acf.info_overview:
Bruntwood SciTech and Select Property Group have a bold vision for Circle Square. One that puts world-class retail and leisure alongside commercial space, residential, student residences and more. But when we got our brief, it was a big empty building site. Our mandate was to increase the local awareness and affinity for what was to come while driving new leads for potential customers.

The ‘Extraordinary Taking Shape’ brand proposition allowed us to celebrate Oxford Road’s groundbreaking past and showcase our vision for its future. We commissioned five artists to produce new works depicting key characteristics of this new neighbourhood within Manchester’s Oxford Road Corridor. We brought them life across a 150ft site hoarding surrounding Circle Square and on digital media. The project delivery also included bespoke website design and build.

acf.caption: Brand Dev
acf.sub_title: A pro experience for kite surfing’s best
acf.summary: Reaching a niche audience that’s radically dedicated to their sport requires a brand with energy to spare. We delivered a brand that captures the epic potential of the WOO Pro and its users.
acf.info_title: A pro experience for kite surfing’s best
acf.info_overview:
WOO Sports needed a brand for its new Pro membership programme that had as much energy as its community. One that reflected the thirst for adventure and achievement that comes with being the best and most ambitious kiters across the world. Their audience was already engaged with the WOO app and sensor, but this pro membership took it to the next level.

With the WOO Pro, the app’s features got a major upgrade — next gen jump analytics, safety features, and new games to play with kiters around the world. ‘Unlock More’ became our rally cry. We called for the community to push themselves to reach new heights, play the game harder, and connect over their shared love of time spent out on the water.

acf.caption: Branding & Ecommerce
acf.summary: While our understanding around the importance of good sleep has progressed, the industry has been left behind. When we were asked to overhaul the architecture of Trendsetter stable of brands we uncovered a new territory and commercial opportunity for them. This Is Sleep is an industry first, tailor made way to buy sleep. Personal, holistic and contemporary for today's consumer.
acf.info_title: Reimagining sleep through insight and innovation
acf.sub_title: Reimagining sleep through insight and innovation
acf.info_overview:
Trendsetter International are a leading bedding brand, with partners including John Lewis and Harrods. They initially tasked us with a strategic brand development project – identifying any new opportunities and reviewing the role and architecture of their current brands.

We started by collaborating with the senior team to define our collective vision and ambition. Through this process we uncovered both a human and commercial insight that lead us to create a new brand that would open up a new opportunity, and allow for a re-structure that would make sense.

Research showed that competition was cluttered but shallow. A flourishing start-up mattress industry was losing steam thanks to too many upstarts and not enough differentiation or personalisation. We uncovered a space for someone with real roots and a diverse heritage in sleep and bedding. One that understands what it takes to get great sleep, as well as it’s importance.

So we created This is Sleep – a new brand offering and total sleep solution, built on product development, sleep theory and the conviction that great sleep is a practice, not a product. Everything was built from scratch, including a complete sleep diagnostic e-commerce system. This focus on the benefits, as well as the holistic and personal, allowed shoppers to understand, nurture and value their sleep.

acf.caption: Healthcare B2B Campaign
acf.summary: Healthcare standards help the NHS save thousands of lives and millions of pounds, and GS1 is the organisation responsible for implementing them. This was a project designed to tell their story, raise voices, inspire engagement and encourage even more action to save even more lives.
acf.info_title: Unlocking the heroes behind NHS standards.

blocks.quote: “We already had an idea of an approach but this completely changed when we engaged with Loaf. Right from the get-go they challenged our ‘traditional’ view and shifted our mindset to think more about the end-user and the impact GS1 standards are having on their lives. I’m so pleased we chose Loaf. Their way of thinking has helped us shift the needle.”
blocks.meta: Alex Smith, Head of Marketing - GS1 UK

acf.sub_title: Unlocking the heroes behind NHS standards.
acf.info_overview:
GS1 needed to make their offering and intentions clear before their national conference. Their success in implementing healthcare standards was undeniable, but the stories didn’t resonate with the power of the change they had created.

The lives of clinicians, CEOs, nurses, pharmacists, and – above all – patients are all directly affected by efficient and universal standards. So why were GS1’s stories feeling disconnected from the real world? We needed the audience to feel as passionate as GS1 did. So we needed something that would inspire them.

We built upon their ‘Global Language of Healthcare’ – with an immersive campaign that our audience could experience online and at the conference. We wanted to empower our healthcare specialists as advocates in their own hospitals. But before hitting them with the facts we had to show that we get them – we see them. The work builds an emotive connection that motivates action – to push for further improvements and GS1 standards throughout the NHS.

acf.summary: A killer destination tucked beneath the Mancunian Way. How do you reach the tastemakers, trend-shakers and harbingers of cool that it was built for? With an attention-grabbing, intrigue-sparking campaign ‘for the curious’.
acf.caption: Hatch Launch Campaign
acf.info_title: Intriguing Manchester’s finest
acf.sub_title: Intriguing Manchester’s finest.
acf.info_overview:
Bruntwood needed footfall and awareness for their newest, coolest retail and leisure destination on the Oxford Road corridor. Sat on a key gateway into Manchester, Hatch is also the entrance to one of their biggest ever projects – Circle Square. So we needed a vision with scale.

A thriving independent retail and leisure scene meant cutting through the noise in traditional ways simply wouldn’t work. Even Bruntwood’s local heavyweight status didn’t extend to consumers. With an audience spoilt for choice, we needed to hook them with something that would genuinely tantalise.

#forthecurious was a campaign built around the target market’s hunger for new discoveries and experiences. Using the shipping containers as design inspiration, we obscured elements of the campaign to create a sense of intrigue and discovery, slowly revealing the location, destination, and offering of Hatch. A non-advertising media solution, utilising fly posters, gorilla tactics and creative activations caught the city’s attention, got our audience talking, engaging, and visiting, and set the tone for further activations.

acf.caption: Grand National Campaign
acf.summary: 2015 was an opportunity to build on our success of the previous year, with a more inclusive look at the thrilling live festival. Our integrated campaign was tailored to help build the reputation and draw in new audiences. To turn the iconic into the unmissable.

blocks.quote: “Loaf has again proved their ability to understand a brief, work in partnership and bring a vision to life with superb creativity. Our aim was to create content that communicates who we are and why it matters in an engaging and shareable way. The result achieves that”
blocks.meta: Scott Bowers, Group Director of Communications - The Jockey Club

acf.info_title: Making the ultimate iconic event even more so.
acf.sub_title: Making the ultimate iconic event even more so.
acf.info_overview:
The development of the stands at Aintree meant that even more tickets were available to sell. This came with an ongoing need to elevate perceptions of the event as a whole.

Even though the Grand National is one of the world’s best-known sporting events, Liverpool folk are spoiled. There’s a lot of leisure on offer in and around the city. Ladies day in particular needed to align with a great girls’ day out. In fact, if there was one day that needed to encapsulate the perfect girls annual get together, it was this.

The festival is a glorious display of unscripted theatre. So we captured the drama of actually being at the festival in a dynamic fashion. With the authenticity and impact of world-famous racing names we brought to life the whole heart-stopping event. Sam Twiston-Davies nailed the anticipation and grandness of Opening Day, while Katie Walsh – riding in couture dress and Louboutin heels – reaffirmed both the excitement and elegance of an all-inclusive Ladies Day owned by the ladies of Liverpool. When the festival began Opening Day crowds were up 4%. Ladies’ Day were up 6%. And Grand National Day was a complete sellout.

get-christmassy.post_title: I think I'm gonna like it here

acf.caption: Christmas Campaign
acf.summary: We found the perfect metaphor for Christmas at Liverpool ONE in the musical Annie. And we used it to create an integrated campaign that captured the magical feeling of the festive season and the joy of shopping. A dazzling cornucopia of Christmas.

blocks.quote: “The team at Loaf demonstrate a great understanding of our brand and the retail industry, delivering strong and stylish creative from concept to fruition and providing valuable strategic insights that help steer the direction of our future marketing activity.”
blocks.meta: Donna Howitt, Marketing & Communications Director - Liverpool ONE

acf.info_title: Capturing a feel good Christmas
acf.homepage_title_override:
I think I'm gonna
like it here
acf.sub_title: Capturing a feel good Christmas
acf.info_overview:
Liverpool ONE is one of Europe’s largest and most iconic outdoor shopping destinations, holding the attention and spend of the region. But with a rapidly evolving retail landscape they still needed to boost footfall and keep discerning shoppers from exploring further afield during Christmas.

Even the heartiest shoppers can find Christmas shopping tedious. What you really want is to spend time with friends and family. Liverpool ONE delivers on both. We just needed a way to show it.

There’s nothing more joyful than a musical, which made it the perfect reflection of the brand’s new ‘Feel Good’ proposition. We looked to the cult classic Annie, and recreated the iconic scene from Daddy Warbucks’ mansion with Liverpool ONE as the fanciful wonderland ripe for exploration. The results were equally upbeat. It beat the previous year by 12.9%, and the national average by 11.2%.

acf.caption: Brand & Website
acf.summary: Genuinely bespoke travel services are hard to find. Our task was to help define then bring to life the vision of two discerning entrepreneurs offering exactly that. Connecting and inspiring their clients. Developing a truly bespoke brand. And delivering the company of their dreams.
acf.info_title: Shaping a truly bespoke travel service.
acf.sub_title: Shaping a truly bespoke travel service.
acf.info_overview:
The fledgling business needed a brand to reflect its unique offering, and the calibre of the knowhow on offer. An online presence would inspire a highly discerning audience. With such a tiny audience, every interaction was critical. A clear, concise, highly personal experience was needed if they were going to start talking about sharing such sensitive data.

Originally they came to us with an email campaign in mind. We knew our response needed to have more impact if we were to genuinely connect their target audience to the importance of the data. We concluded that the best way to make them appreciate the true scale of multiple data streams was to show them.

We built a dynamic 3D WebGL particle engine called ‘Data Turbine’ – a technical, data-driven digital experience that delivered the message in a dynamic and deeply engaging way. emotionlab.author: Head of Technology - Andy Buchan

emotionlab.post_content:
The landscape we operate in and what clients need from a creative partner is radically changing, and in turn, our approach has had to evolve. Psychology, data, technology, and innovation are now just as big a part of what we do as the craft and production values that we made our name with. There is a near-constant tension in the advertising industry about our role in people’s lives. We often see ourselves solving problems, finding new solutions, and ultimately, selling — but to what end? This thought is behind our shift towards brand experience. And it’s more than just a buzzword. For us, brand experience is about meeting people where they are. Seeing how the brand interacts with the rest of their life. And ultimately making your brand present in innovative, appropriate, and impactful ways. 

Context matters. Customer journeys are changing and we need to make sure that every touchpoint is one that moves and motivates the customer to act. The brands that succeed are ones who put in the work — because a strong brand foundation is the most important step in working towards a consistent, engaging, and effective brand experience. If you look to the direct-to-consumer successes from the past 10 years, many have been enabled by the unfettered access to their audiences. Need advice on product development? A testbed of 100k is only an Instagram post away. For brands with a clear vision, it’s an easy win. 

That quick win isn’t often replicated by brands who were grandfathered into this digital age. The winners win because it’s natural. The same goes for purpose. Those who succeed with pro-social messaging do so because it’s organic. Every touchpoint is an experience. Every interaction and relationship counts. We believe that brands that commit to engaging people with more empathy and emotion at every opportunity create better brand experiences and more desirable brands. Thankfully, it doesn’t have to be a revolution. It all starts with intent. And this is a space where iterative improvements result in measurable results. 

But the more things change, the more they stay the same. Which is why at the heart of what we do, still remains the drive to deliver work that makes people feel something. Work that motivates people to do something. Work that is beautiful.

emotionlab.author: MD/Co-founder – Alan Houghton

emotionlab.post_content:
Augmented reality isn't anything new but as an agency we're always looking for ways (old and new) to leverage technology and activate brands in more interesting ways. One of the core challenges that existed for AR was the lack of audience. In order for brands to launch an AR experience they were required to create their own mobile application and distribute it. Both significant challenges to launching tactical experiences.

Instagram (well Facebook) to the rescue! Over the past 12 months both platforms have rolled and evolved a series of Augmented Reality features that allow to do more than just face filters and bunny ears. These extensions to Facebook messenger and Instagram now give brands an audience instantly at no cost and without any of the friction attached to downloading an app. Given that in the UK alone Instagram has 25 million active users we can step over all of the previous logistical challenges.

So what does it mean when any brand can deploy an AR experience to a huge audience with little media spend? Well part of what we do here at LOAF and in our Emotion Lab is to think about meaningful applications for technology. Not technology for technologies sake. So no, we're not launching more bunny ears of dog face filters (sorry). We apply and blend our technical understanding with our experience methodology to define opportunities and establish the potential for brands.

With that in mind we applied our thinking towards one of our favourite clients, Bruntwood, who are one of the UK's largest property developers. One of their largest developments, right at the heart of Manchester is Circle Square - a beautiful new mixed use neighbourhood doing extraordinary in and around the city. We worked with bruntwood on the place making of this new district and destination

Bringing to life the core proposition of ‘extraordinary taking shape’, we wanted to test out these new AR abilities through instagram - so we set out to bring to life elements of a hoarding design we had done a few months previous.

What we learned

A hoarding may not be the perfect place the the use of AR, at least not in this location. Circle square is based right in the middle of Manchester’s Oxford road, a road with a heavy footfall and also parallel to a main road. However, the ability to engage further with customers, through platforms they use everyday is mightily exciting, and begins to shift what can be done when the barriers for engagement are reduced.

Movement, animation and textures takes AR to the next level - and we will be experimenting further soon.

acf.sub_title: Old media, new media

emotionlab.author: Head of Technology - Andy Buchan

emotionlab.post_content:
“Typography is the craft of endowing human language with a durable visual form.”
? Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style

Often the craft of typography sits in conflict with its durability. As media evolves, type must move with it to make sure it’s fit for purpose. Thankfully, technology is catching up to empower designers to satisfy their creative desires without abandoning the evolving accessibility and responsive demands of modern design. Variable font technology enables brands to tweak their font to improve customer touch points throughout their brand experience — whether that is accessibility, expression or immersive digital experiences.

A variable font is a font that behaves like several fonts, in one single file rather than multiple files. Presently, when a user visits a web page, each individual font file has to be downloaded to show the text. Variable fonts are an evolving technology that offer creative control, with great benefits to accessibility, usability, and flexibility.

Accessible design is good design. With an ageing population and evolving technology, there is no reason not to design for all. Everyone should have access to good design. With variable fonts, type can be adjusted to increase legibility or adjusted to its environment. The changing conditions around the user (low light, for example) could prompt a subtle shift in weight with significant benefits. As people spend more and more time in front of screens, brands should work to make their experience as palatable as possible. One size fits all typography doesn’t work for brands and it doesn’t work for consumers. These benefits to accessibility are just the beginning. There is so much potential for immersive, expressive, and responsive typography.

One of the biggest trends for 2020 is a strong move towards type-only creative solutions. As designers innovate with bold, decorative type, they are pushing the boundaries of modern design. But even type purists can admit that poin`t size carries weight. Iconic designer Massimo Vignelli once said “You can say, "I love you," in Helvetica. And you can say it with Helvetica Extra Light if you want to be really fancy. Or you can say it with the Extra Bold if it's really intensive and passionate.” With variable fonts, you could personalise the experience and prompt an emotional response of your audience. A signature weight of your brand’s font offers another level of distinctiveness.

There are effectiveness benefits to a type-only approach as well. Single minded statements are memorable and efficient. Pair that with the creative potential of variable fonts, there’s no reason to let this trend pass us by. Interactive digital experiences, apps, and gaming offer opportunities as well.

Variable fonts allow you to control your brand experience and increases brand equity, recognisability, and better user experience. They are still an early technology so support for it is limited but the potential is there. The impact on brand experience alone is enough for us to pay attention. Watch this space because the future fonts are coming.

emotionlab.author: Zak Rains – Creative

emotionlab.post_content:
Music plays a huge part in my life. Whether that’s releasing some energy on the drums, plugging in on my commute or tuning out on the living room sofa – music inspires me. It changes my mood, it makes me feel alive. The power of music is inescapable – it’s one of the biggest channels of entertainment in the world, and a key aspect of virtually every other one. Film wouldn’t be film without music. Neither would gaming. Music is an expression of emotion for its composer, creating an emotional and cultural connection with any listener.

But what about the power of sound – the elemental foundation of music? Sound has been used to heal for thousands of years. It’s used in other positive and therapeutic ways all over the world, and its benefits to health and wellbeing are truly exciting.

But it’s a power that’s still largely invisible in the world of brand. It’s under-exploited and under-explored, and essentially non-existent in many brand planning documents. Sound design and sonic branding aren’t new, but with a new wave of research and development in the field, more brands are beginning to realise how sound can have a profound effect across countless touchpoints.

Sound can rouse emotions and connect in ways the other senses can’t. From Skype re-designing their 'loader sound' to make the app feel quicker and more agile to ‘The sound of HSBC’, an entire sonic brand developed by the bank in collaboration with musician Jean-Michel Jarre, brands are utilising sound more and more. And they’re working harder to understand how they can harness all that power.

Going deeper

Since sound is vital to our work in honing brand experiences, we’re looking at it more closely than ever at present, especially the ways that different sounds and frequencies effect mood and emotions.

Most recently, our whole team embraced a ’Sonic Healing’ session, designed by Neil Davis, Director of City Therapy and active proponent of the power of sound. Neil has been delivering sonic experiences all over the world for the past five years, for names such as Above & Beyond. His approach is based on re-aligning the vibrations that emanate from every atom in every molecule in your body, and the experience was as surprising as it was enjoyable.

I had never experienced sound in this raw, focused way before. With nothing to look at, and no triggers nudging me to ‘feel’ something specific, the sense was elevated and incredibly powerful. From the sound of Tibetan singing bowls and osteophonic tuning forks, to native flutes, buffalo, ocean drums and electronic beats, the result was a cascading journey of emotions and feelings. Emerging from the session we all agreed that the feeling was akin to meditation, albeit with a sense of relaxation and fresh focus.

As different as the experience was, it certainly reflected my own personal connection with music and sound, and the essential truth that human beings have utilised for centuries – that there is something unique about the way sound impacts us. With the explosion of voice technology and the speedy development of utilities across most sectors, it’s clear that defining what a brand sounds like should now be as important as defining how it looks and behaves. 

Sound matters. It powerfully affects customer experience, attitudes and behaviour. It shapes moods and – more importantly – can help define strong emotional connections about a brand, product and service choice.

So if you’ve not started to develop your brands sonic strategy, and how your brand sounds, now might be a good time to start.

emotionlab.author: Creative Director / Co-founder – Dave Mullen

emotionlab.post_content:
We spend a lot of time in the studio thinking about emotion. What makes an impact? What makes you feel? But more often than not, what we’re after is a memory. We want to connect our clients’ brands and products to an emotional memory; to prompt a cognitive snapshot that cements the brand story in precious brain space.

This month’s Campaign Magazine focus is Memory, and we spent an afternoon in London at the Campaign Underground Focal Recall event seeing just how memory plays into what we do. From leveraging nostalgia to amplifying sensory interactions, we learned the true potential of memory as a key player in the proposition, planning, and delivery phases of creative work.

Loaf’s strategic process is rooted in understanding the customer’s motivations and unpacking their assumptions. Dr Amy Milton, of the University of Cambridge, spoke passionately about the true purpose of memory as a force to serve us in the future, as a teacher and a guide. If it wasn’t there to lead us, we’d all be drinking our coffee out of a shoe and walking down dark alleys without a care in the world.

For better and worse, memory is imperfect and can change over time. The more emotion you experience during an event, the stronger the memory is; but more often than not, it’s also inaccurate. These inaccuracies can provoke and strengthen implicit biases which play a large part in the consumer journey. Familiarity breeds preference, so if we’re trying to break consumer patterns we have to form new emotional connections that override their existing assumptions.

From the five hours we spent immersed in memory, these are only a few of the ideas that planted in our long-term memory and we’ll certainly be using them to map out our future, and the future of our work.

emotionlab.author: Creative Director / Co-founder – Dave Mullen

emotionlab.post_content:
My pursuit of innovation in the brand communications world. 

Innovation is widely banded about as the hip way to label your brand ‘futuristic.’ It’s a way to ‘differentiate’ yourself within the sector. Bolt on the terms AI, Blockchain and VR in your presentation and you're in with the Silicon Valley tribe. In all seriousness, innovation means different things to different people; yet, it can have profound impact on brand growth if you understand it and invest in it. To innovate is to;  “action to make changes in something established, especially by introducing new methods, ideas, or products.” We all want to innovate to a degree. It speaks to the desire to not sit still and results in quicker successes and a more robust future for your company. However, to really innovate effectively requires a certain mindset and dedication from the top down, across the organisation.

Following a recent 2 day trip to the innovation event Unbound London, I couldn’t stop thinking about the focus across most of the talks: the how to of innovation. One talk in particular satirised the subject and, focussed on how not to innovate. Follow their 8 tips and innovation will shut down quickly within your organisation! Comedy aside, the point of the talk was spot on.

Why are we all not innovating now? Most brands really want to, but they don’t know how to, and if they try, they often treat it as a siloed off department. 

What does innovation mean to Loaf?

As an agency, we are innovating across every department. Be it production, ideation, operations, finance, or client services; it’s a mindset we strive to embed into our culture across the board. To encourage curiosity, exploration, and the freedom to never accept the ‘normal way of doing things.’ It’s our way of innovating as a business. We take this approach directly to brands to influence the way they look at campaigns and brand customer experience. Our ambition is to explore new avenues in brand product, service, and customer acquisition. This results in the birth of new products, services, and communications that forge new kinds of relationships with new kinds of customers.

So, How do you Innovate?

The first step is to set requirements and keep to them. This is essential to make innovation productive for your business. 

Freedom

Innovation has to come from the heart of an organisation. It cannot be pushed to one side or department, it cannot be explored under usual business restraints, it cannot have a clear business plan, and it cannot guarantee a ROI. Freedom is absolutely necessary across an organisation’s structure to openly encourage innovation through brand, product, or service. The best innovations are born from open collaboration, so it cannot be forced upon under usual business processes.

Curiosity

Adopt a curious mindset. Innovation leaders must naturally have the urge and desire to explore and experiment. The curiosity mindset is one of confidence in not accepting the norm. Rory Sutherland of Ogilvy Change reciprocates this, by stating “if there were a logical answer, we would have already found it”. 

Define a Singular Challenge

Too often, innovators attempt to climb Everest and take on the world. Innovation is about failing fast, learning, and taking the chance to succeed greatly. Listen to your customers and give them what they desire. Just Eat started by noticing obsessive gamers couldn’t leave their computers, yet wanted takeaways delivered upstairs... in the same building! Solve one problem at a time through exploration and curiosity, and build on it. Walk up one mountain at a time. 

Innovation should be focussed on how we can solve or pursue a challenge in different ways. Too often, I see people innovating by playing catch up with the competition. Express freedom in your thinking and take inspiration from completely different sectors, cultures, and trends. Think about where you are going, not where you are.

The Perfect Recipe

So, how do we innovate successfully? 

Innovation is easily, and quickly, shut down, as it demands that we abandon traditional methods and encourage a culture of curiosity. Rory Sutherland summarises the perfect recipe of innovation: “The best innovation happens at the intersection of complexity economics, technology and (evolutionary) psychology.”
Now go forth and explore the world, expand your mindset, explode the norm, fall down, get up better, and in the end, innovate.

emotionlab.author: Innovation Director – Tom Downing

emotionlab.post_content:
The decline of the highstreet has been well reported. The stats are clear but what isn’t is the cause. I’ve recently spent some time thinking about placemaking and the future of retail, and there are some fundamental insights and solutions out there. 

What can we do to keep bricks-and-mortar shopping desirable and who is to blame for this decline in the high st? There is no doubt that it’s heavily impacted by the surge of online, but it’s the place that holds the power. Retailers want to be in desirable places that offer a sound business case. Town centres across the country need to develop a place that people actually want to visit. I recently heard how Barnsley town centre is working with architects who have a clear vision for their future. They’re working to develop the downtrodden and unattractive town centre and create a place where it is an enjoyable experience to visit. 

With a strong high street, once you add in a leisure centre and a library, a sense of community is borne. There’s a meeting place for people to love, a place for people to belong, and a place that’s unique to the people of the area. More needs to be done by the councils to show a greater vision. They need to be responsible for placemaking. And it is the retailers task of making their offering something people want to come and experience, across all consumer touchpoints. From the moment they walk in, they should be immersed in the brand, not just the products they sell. Customer service and interactions are key to creating memorability and recall and these are things that some of the more well known high st brands have failed to embrace and they have since suffered the consequences. 

There are leaders in the pack that retailers can look to for inspiration. Adidas has a shop/workspace in London diversifying their offer and creating a meeting place and reason to visit the shop that’s not just about buying their products. Rapha has introduced a clubhouse space to hang out in their London store. Both of these activities speak directly to the values and community-building goals of the brands. It’s about experiencing the brand, and its values, across every touchpoint. There have also been moves over the last few years by companies such as Mercedes - building experiential stores in retail spaces not typically associated with the automotive industry, that allow potential customers that would never walk into a showroom, to experience Mercedes products and services with no extra effort. It is a real glimpse into how these spaces could develop in the future.

Also, we can’t forget about the independents. The NQ in Manchester is the 2nd most visited place in the city centre with its vast choice of shops, restaurants, and bars all offering a nicer experience to the chains that you may get elsewhere in the city. Independents excel at defining their brand purpose and creating desirable spaces for their target consumers because they have to. It’s the key to distinctiveness. It is great to see so many of these independents now making a mark on the retail landscape. 

So, is it as bleak as it seems? The numbers aren’t proving as sensational as the headlines promise but this trend should be seen as an opportunity. It's about diversification. It’s about using the physical space to its full potential. It’s about innovating and looking to the future. What you cannot do online is interact, spend time, shop and eat with friends and family, but most importantly touch, feel, taste and try for yourself. It's about the right mix of activity. Every brand should embrace the physical and digital activations of their brand, to ensure that each and every time a consumer comes into contact you’re adding to their overall experience. It's about knowing who you are, what your brand stands for and why consumers should care - then offering an experience that matches that. It’s down to the retailers, and the places themselves, to innovate and evolve to match consumer demand, whilst offering difference, and new reasons to visit - some of which the consumer won’t even know they want yet.

As the saying goes: what got you here, won’t get you there.

emotionlab.post_content:
There is so much hype around voice assistants. Duly so given the opportunities, but I cannot help think brands are missing a trick when it comes to making real emotive, purpose-driven voice experiences.

Alexa and Google have one voice. You can distinguish your skill by adding hints of personality in the form of polys, but really, we all hear and picture one personality. Too often I see technology used by brands with a pure tech-driven motive. In order to be truly effective when it comes to consumer engagement, the story has to start from the brand's personality.

During the launch of a new Voice group Voice2, founded by VCCP’s Innovation Lead Will Harvey and ex head of Emerging Platforms & Partnerships team at Lego James Poulter, conversations were about just this. For brands to take voice seriously, they need to look at sonic branding and factor it into their wider long-term brand development. A brand’s voice is just that, a piece of identity it should own and be recognised for. What does Ford sound like compared to Honda? 

The real trick is to start with a brand experience perspective. Find the brand narrative that intertwines with a valuable voice experience idea. Get experts who live and breathe brand tone of voice - copywriters, brand strategists AND technologists in one room. These are the people that should be exploring the early stages of a brands voice skill project. Work out how to take your audience on a journey that feels like it’s relevant to your brand.  

This is the process we take via our Emotion Lab, a discovery space for us to collaborate with brands to explore what it means to innovate outside the realms of normal marketing comms restraints. The adoption rate of voice assistants has overtaken the uptake of smartphones. This alone shows how as a society worldwide, we want to use our voice more and more. We, as brands leaders, just have to work out our role in all this.

The future is so exciting for voice with untapped opportunities yet to be explored.

emotionlab.author: Innovation Director – Tom Downing

emotionlab.post_content:
Purpose is the answer. Purpose is dead. Who cares about purpose? All we care about is purpose. When Jim Stengel laid out the idea of ‘Brand Ideal’ in his book Grow, the advertising industry bought-in for a pound. Surely this was the silver bullet. The best way to build emotional resonance and get customers to associate the brand with all that glitters and the gold. 

Unfortunately, most of the people who bought-in saw it as a business tool, rather than a passion-filled, action-fueling life force. On Stengal’s website, he proudly declares: “The surest path to growth – pursue an aim greater than profit.” This in itself is absurd—the surest path to growth—measured by profit—is to pursue an aim greater than profit. So, if we want to transform stagnant brands, all we need an altruistic band-aid. 

Behavioural science specialist Richard Shotton categorised this bias as ‘wishful seeing’ in his book, The Choice Factory.  “Agencies have been guilty of promoting theories of advertising that they want to be true,” wrote Shotton, “rather than ones that actually are true.” And the beauty of brand purpose is that it is actually both. It can be a vehicle for wishful seeing, but it can also be an incredibly powerful motivator for consumers. 

The trick is not aligning your purpose with your values, it's aligning your purpose with your product. Having a broader goal is only effective when it matches with the goals of your end customer. By self-identifying as a member of the target audience, rather than an external force, every action taken to boost the confidence of the audience, boosts the confidence in the brand. Sociologist William Sumner noted that “each group nourishes its own pride and vanity, boasts itself superior, exists in its own divinities, and looks with contempt on outsiders,” and while this notion is historically at the root of most political conflicts, we, as wishful seeing advertisers, can see the value in grounding strategies in this theory. 

Behaviour is at the root of any great communications strategy. Our messaging goals are always rooted in prompting, halting, or shifting a behaviour. Where we, as advertisers, need to do better, is in understanding the product, independent of its grand ambitions or sordid past, to understand why it was created. If we dig and dig and dig— and at the bottom of the pile—still find pure profit and practicality, perhaps it’s time to shelf brand purpose for that case.

emotionlab.author: Head of strategy – Sarah Joynt-Bowe

emotionlab.post_content:
We, like many other businesses and our clients, have been facing the challenge of keeping sales continuous whilst delivering an uninterrupted experience and service during the outbreak of Covid-19. It’s clear that we are all yet to discover our new norm, as the world learns how to adapt to our adjusted lifestyles.

Our recent tilt in focus as an agency to brand experience, both improving and unifying it, has exposed us to more relevant and more important questions about what our clients actually need, what we as a creative agency are actually here to do, and what the value of this work is.

Over the last few weeks we have been working with our clients to understand how their brand experiences can be maintained, whilst their ability to connect and engage with their audience is being put to the test. With the focus of attention quite rightly on the health and wellbeing of family and loved ones - the concerns of our clients are real - how do they best align with their customers and spend budgets effectively now and over the coming months.

Our aim is to share our experience and creative expertise to provide solutions that are both swift and insightful. We believe there are a range of new opportunities available for brands to strengthen their visibility and conversion - whilst also helping to build their brand for the future.

Our experience in helping brands better engage with customers has allowed us to hone in on the challenges our clients are currently facing, and support them in a range of different ways. We have learned a lot in the last few weeks, and we wanted to share some of our thoughts and opinions on what brands should be considering in relation to their brand experience…

Don’t expect ‘normal’
As the lockdown eases, some of the more successful changes in how we work and live will be here to stay. Many consumers won’t want the old ‘normal’, so it’s essential brands really understand what people actually want. Many may find that this is very different to what their insight and research of the past suggests.

Change gear with content
With the increased amount of time consumers are spending online, brands need to seize the opportunity to be more present. There should be a focus on producing a range of relevant content that is based on storytelling and adding value to lives, not just gaining likes and sales. This more than ever, is a time to stand out from the crowd.

Create more engaging online destinations
Digital media has quickly become a leader in enabling social interactions and sales. Social distancing and limitations in place restrict the ability to meet your customers face to face and engage in person. From shopping on the high street to viewing properties, the needs and expectations of online experiences have risen - and every online touchpoint needs be unique, memorable and useful.

Be open with your agency
Relationships are essential to success. Now is the time to sit down with your creative agency and openly discuss the challenges your company is facing right now. A good creative agency will listen, be honest about the issues it can help with, and work with you to solve them.

Have a plan
This sounds obvious, but this is a very unique situation that requires a unique plan. Even if your activity is already predominantly digital, a shift in focus and how you interact is important to be relevant in the current market. What was important to consumers a month ago, may not be so important now.

Stay safe everyone.
